analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. It bumps the date and adds an 'Add-on hold busy fields' section (head lines 172-195). It adds a register-table row for busy_reason/busy_since_ms/busy_addon (head line 284). Another changed range is at head 383, and one at 1445, which falls in the base 1418 busy_reason vocabulary area. Neither of these two ranges was visible in the supplied units, since the head text stops at line 325 and the base text runs 1230-1546. No executable code or controls changed.

Security-relevant claims in the new text:
- A held provider reports heartbeat.status=draining with provider-supplied busy fields.
- The hold never sends provider_drain, so the connection is not fenced.
- The hold returns on the same connection with the next idle/serving heartbeat.
- A coordinator that ignores the busy fields still stops routing on the draining status.

I see no regression against the TB-002 or TB-011 assumptions:
- The busy fields are provider-controlled, self-reported, closed-vocabulary hints. They cannot grant serving authorization, because the text states routing is excluded while draining.
- Resuming on the same connection via a heartbeat is a status change only. Authorization, final-handoff rechecks (authorizeInferenceHandoff) and App Attest grants are unaffected per the cited TB-002/TB-011 text. The doc does not claim a hold clears a drain barrier or revocation fence.
- A malicious provider (ADV-001) could omit or forge busy fields or report idle at will, but that is already within its control and only affects its own availability.

Open integration questions the next pass could check against unseen code, such as ProviderBusy.swift and buildHeartbeatFrame:
- Whether heartbeat 'idle' after a hold cannot override a coordinator-side drain fence or a provider_drain barrier.
- Whether busy_addon (an untrusted string) is length-bounded or sanitized on the coordinator before logging or admin display. The doc does not specify this, so I do not treat it as a finding.

The threat model may eventually need a note on add-on holds, but nothing here invalidates an existing assumption.
